guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case is less about Kansas being the better team and more about its ability to create enough scoring opportunities to stay inside the market’s expectation. Our longer-run numbers view Kansas’ offense more favorably than Arizona State’s ability to prevent those opportunities. Kansas’ opener offers some supporting context rather than proof: Isaiah Marshall produced 246 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and 49 rushing yards in his second career start, while Nik McMillan added 130 receiving yards and a touchdown in his Kansas debut.

We also see reasons to believe that production can remain functional against stronger competition. Kansas allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss in the opener, giving Marshall time to access an offense with both passing-game explosiveness and quarterback mobility. The meaningful concern is on the other side, where our efficiency numbers identify Kansas’ pass defense as the matchup Arizona State is best positioned to challenge. Even with that vulnerability, we think the market is asking Kansas to lose by a wider margin than the overall matchup warrants.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We will be watching Arizona State’s passing offense against Kansas’ secondary. Kansas brought back starting cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander and free safety Taylor Davis, and its 2025 defense allowed its fewest passing yards per game since 2001. Our current efficiency numbers are less flattering, however, so the question is whether that returning experience can keep Arizona State from consistently turning favorable passing situations into scoring chances. That is the clearest threat to our position.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, including 277 rushing yards and 336 passing yards.
Kansas rushed for five touchdowns against Long Island; Yasin Willis led the team with 72 yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and no touchdowns.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss against Long Island, including a career-high four by Leroy Harris III.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State opened the 2026 season with a 70-7 win over Morgan State and was 1-0 entering its Sept. 12 game at Texas A&M.
Kansas and Arizona State are scheduled to open Big 12 play against each other on Sept. 19, 2026 at Wembley Stadium in London.

quarterback.fact: Head coach Lance Leipold named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall Kansas' starting quarterback before the 2026 season.
In his second career start, Isaiah Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Backup Cole Ballard completed 4 of 6 passes for 90 yards in the season opener and has two career starts listed through Game 1 of 2026.
Chase Jenkins joined Kansas after starting all 12 regular-season games for Rice in 2025, when he passed for 1,025 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 531 yards and five touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas' Game 2 offensive line listed Calvin Clements at left tackle, Amir Herring at left guard, Kasen Carpenter at center, Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard and Nick Morrow at right tackle.
Clements and Herring are the two returning offensive-line starters from 2025; each started all 12 games that season.
New center Kasen Carpenter transferred after starting two games for Oklahoma State in 2025 and 11 games for Tulsa in 2024.
New right tackle Nick Morrow arrived from California after starting five games in 2025.
Transfer receiver Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in his Kansas debut against Long Island, extending his streak of 100-yard receiving games to seven.
Kansas' running-back depth chart listed transfers Dylan Edwards and Yasin Willis as co-starters, followed by transfer Jalen Dupree.
Against Long Island, Edwards rushed six times for 32 yards, Willis rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns, and Dupree rushed nine times for 35 yards and one touchdown.

defensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returned five defensive starters from 2025: linebacker Trey Lathan, cornerbacks Austin Alexander and Jalen Todd, safety Taylor Davis and defensive tackle Blake Herold.
Trey Lathan returned after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Transfer defensive end David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery against Long Island.
Kansas' Game 2 secondary listed returning starters Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander at cornerback and Taylor Davis at free safety, with transfer Corey Gordon at strong safety.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after two seasons at Penn State; he previously served as Kansas' offensive coordinator from 2021 through 2023.
D.K. McDonald remained Kansas' defensive coordinator for the 2026 season, his third season with the program.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett did not play in Kansas' season opener against Long Island.
Pickett was listed as a co-starter with Keaton Kubecka on Kansas' Game 2 depth chart.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas' offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
Kansas generated six plays of at least 20 yards, including three plays of at least 40 yards, against Long Island.
Kansas has allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest total in the Big 12 over that span.
Kansas averaged 19.7 yards per completion over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, the highest figure in the Big 12 over that period.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, fourth in the Big 12.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, punter Matt Gill from Australia and long snapper Rino Monteforte from California for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
Kansas' Game 2 depth chart listed Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner.

series_context.fact: Arizona State leads the series with Kansas 1-0 after defeating the Jayhawks 35-31 in Tempe in 2024.
The 2026 meeting will be the first Kansas-Arizona State game played in London.

other_relevant.fact: The Kansas-Arizona State game will be Kansas' first international football game and the first college football game played at Wembley Stadium.
Kansas will face Missouri on Sept. 11 before playing Arizona State in London on Sept. 19; Arizona State will visit Texas A&M on Sept. 12 before the Kansas game.
